title: What If You Never Took a Vacation?

scenes.text: What if you never took a single vacation? Your heart would keep the score.
Scientists tracked twelve thousand American men at high risk of heart disease for nine years.
The men who took a vacation every year were about a third less likely to die of heart disease.
In Finland, a study followed a group of executives for thirty years.
Those who took three weeks off a year or less had a 37 percent higher chance of dying.
It's a link, not proof. But the trip you keep skipping may cost more than the ticket.

description:
A study of 12,338 middle-aged American men from the MRFIT heart trial found that those who took annual vacations were about 21% less likely to die of any cause and 32% less likely to die of coronary heart disease over nine years.
In the Helsinki Businessmen Study, men in one group who took three weeks or less of annual vacation had a 37% greater chance of dying between 1974 and 2004. Both studies show associations, not cause and effect.
